text:
sasha: Quick thread — I'm proposing we change our admission control from the current single-mode (queue until timeout) to a hybrid: immediate reject for gold latency-SLO routes, degrade (fallback to smaller quantized model) for silver, and queue with short token-budget for bronze/background. Reason: recent spikes hit 90% GPU packing in us-west and the queue latency is killing p99 for gold users.

ryan: +1 on hybrid. Curious: how do we pick thresholds? currently it's just max_queue_ms global.

maria: We should tie it to estimated GPU-seconds per request and current backlog. For example if estimated gpu-ms + backlog_gpu_ms > window we start rejecting for gold.

tony: Important: network tail (nvlink saturation) also exacerbates tail latency. If we only look at GPU occupancy we'll still see p99 blips. Need a composite metric: gpu_util + net_tail_percentile.

ryan: Agree. Also want to preserve fairness across regions — can't have us-west rejecting while eu-central queues forever because of capacity differences.

sasha: Proposed config (v0):
```yaml
admission:
  classes:
    gold:
      mode_priority: [reject, degrade]
      max_queue_ms: 50
      fallback_model: "redwood-compact-v1"
    silver:
      mode_priority: [degrade, queue]
      max_queue_ms: 200
      fallback_model: "redwood-small-v2"
    bronze:
      mode_priority: [queue]
      max_queue_ms: 1000
  metrics_used: ["gpu_estimated_ms","gpu_util_1m","nvlink_tail_95","region_capacity_index"]
  region_smoothing_window_s: 60
  rejection_ratio_target: 0.02  # try to keep rejects under 2% for gold overall
```

maria: This looks sensible. For rollout we should canary in a single AZ first (us-west-2a) and only for non-critical routes, then expand to whole region.

tony: Also define explicit rollback criteria: if gold p99 latency increases by >5% or error rate increase >0.5% within 30m post-rollout, immediately revert.

ryan: How will we surface per-customer behavior? ops needs to see when a tenant is getting degraded vs rejected.

sasha: We'll emit an admission_event with fields: class, action (queue/degrade/reject), reason, estimated_gpu_ms, region, tenant_id. Example: `admission_event{class=gold,action=degrade,reason=high_gpu_util,est_ms=120,region=us-west,tenant=acme}`. We'll hook this into Console traces.

deploy-bot: Deploy queued: admission-controller:v0.3 will be deployed to us-west-2a at 2026-03-18T14:22Z during canary window.

ops-oncall: Can you also add alerting on admission_event.rate > baseline + 3sigma for gold? We saw a silent steady reject stream last month.

maria: Good call. Add a dashboard: admissions by action over time, percent of requests per class that were degraded/rejected, and p99 latency per action.

sasha: Cost note: degrading to smaller models reduces GPU-seconds per request ~3-4x but increases token-level cost for some responses (more decoding). Net should still be cheaper than full rejects + retries. We'll monitor cost per inference graph.

ryan: Question: do we want automated fallback chaining? e.g., gold -> fallback small -> fallback tiny -> reject. Could be good but risky for hallucination/regression.

tony: If we chain, must bind to eval sets: fallback models must pass a minimum QA for each route. Otherwise we risk regressions.

maria: Ops playbook update: when we see >5% degraded for a tenant for >15m, page on-call and include link to console filtered by tenant. For rejects, immediate page if rate exceeds 1 req/s sustained for 5m.

sasha: Rollout plan summary: 1) Canary in us-west-2a for non-critical routes (24h), 2) Expand to region but keep gold rejects capped at 1% (48h), 3) Full rollout with alerts and runbook (1 week). Revert if rollback criteria hit.

ryan: LGTM. I can implement admission controller changes and the telemetry hooks. Want me to also add a simulation job to run synthetic spike tests?

sasha: Yes please — add a k8s cron job that replays production-like trace samples with overload multiplier and validates that the controller decisions follow expectations. Save simulation output to s3 and post results in #eng-infra.

tony: One more: ensure dedicated pools (reserved capacity customers) get priority bump in the controller so they rarely degrade. That impacts cost/alloc but is contractual.

maria: I'll update the ensure_policy_tests and add unit tests for decision boundaries.

sasha: Thanks all. I'll open the PR with the config and rollout steps, tag @ryan and @maria. :thumbsup:
